prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant topological insulator and quantum spin Hall effect, and its experimental discovery in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B044 as a single-part prize to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. After the full first-round exchange the scientific case has not weakened: the Z2 classification identified a symmetry-protected state of matter, the quantum spin Hall edge channels were predicted, and quantised edge conductance was then measured in HgTe quantum wells and reproduced by independent groups over about two decades with a stable interpretation. It is a discovery of a nameable phenomenon in nature, which is the first step in how I think the committee should work, and only afterwards do we ask who is responsible. Four of eight members prefer it, and the chair's summary shows no one calling it premature or unconfirmed. What I have changed is the wording, not the configuration. Eriksson, Johansson and Olsson tie the experiment to HgTe quantum wells, and the chair asks for a citation that neither claims the three-dimensional work nor ignores the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. My round-1 phrasing, 'topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect', was broader than the credited names can support, so I now propose the narrower HgTe-based wording. That answers the chair's first question: the citation names what these three did and claims nothing for Fu, Moore, Balents, Roy or Hasan.
statement.case_against: The credit remains incomplete. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe/CdTe as the platform that Molenkamp measured, and the three-dimensional topological insulator work is outside the credited set. Three names is the maximum and the protocol does not let me add a fourth, so the omission is a limit of the prize structure and I will not pretend it away. I am also aware that a committee which treats a missing proposer as disqualifying would reasonably prefer B024, where two names fit the claim exactly. I do not hold that view, because Kane and Mele's prediction and Molenkamp's observation are the two ends of the discovery and the proposal that connected them, though important, is the one link that falls outside the supplied names. A secondary objection is overlap with the 2016 prize, which I judge weak since the 2016 citation concerned topological phase transitions and Hall-type topological phases, while time-reversal-invariant insulators without a magnetic field are a different class.

responses.point: Lindroth treats the unresolved Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and three-dimensional attribution, together with the 2016 prize, as reasons to put the clean two-name B024 ahead of B044.
responses.response: I accept that B024 has the cleaner credit and I do not dispute its maturity or its distinctness from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, which your invention-and-realisation wording makes clear. But I read the attribution gap as a limit of a three-name prize and not a disqualifier. If we required a complete credit chain we would rarely award a prize with a theory and an experiment part at all. Narrowing the citation to the prediction and the HgTe observation removes the claim to the three-dimensional work that you worry about. On 2016, the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall edge were not what Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz were recognised for, so I do not see the novelty as absorbed. I would change my view if someone shows that the 2016 citation or its scientific background already covers time-reversal-invariant insulators, but I do not think that can be shown.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the lattice clock's roughly two-orders-of-magnitude capability gain directly produces new phenomena, so a measurement invention can outrank a nameable phenomenon in nature.
responses.response: That is a fair argument and I do not regard an invention as lesser than a discovery. My difficulty is with the evidence for the claim. Lindroth rightly says that what has been delivered is a capability at the 1e-18 level, and the tests of constants and dark matter so far set limits, so the argument for new physics is still prospective. For B044 the physical result is in hand: a measured, quantised edge conductance and a whole materials programme built on it. I also take Kroll's point that I should not use my own distance from the field to dismiss his, and I keep B024 as my first alternative. If the committee prefers it, I could support it with the invention-and-realisation citation that Lindroth and Pearce propose.

responses.point: Olsson would keep the Kane-Mele core intact and say so in the citation if the committee cannot resolve the theory credit, and argues that the Molenkamp experiment was the first direct evidence of the predicted state.
responses.response: I agree and I have adopted this in the citation. Without the experiment the Kane-Mele prediction would remain a theoretical proposal, and the HgTe result is why the committee can speak of a discovery. I am less sure than you that the Kane-Mele core can stand without the BHZ proposal in the narrative, since the chain from prediction to measurement ran through HgTe. I would therefore keep the wording to what the three credited people did, and leave the committee's text to record that the platform was proposed by others, rather than try to give them credit that the name limit does not allow.

responses.point: Mehlig argues that the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap in B044 is a difficulty comparable to the Crooks omission in B016, and that clean credit should be weighed against how fundamental the result is.
responses.response: I take the comparison seriously, but the two cases differ in what is missing. In B016 any three of the four names omits someone whose result is nearly equivalent to a credited one, so the choice among Jarzynski, Evans, Crooks and Seifert is genuinely contested, as Eriksson also says. In B044 the credited three are the predictor of the effect, its co-predictor and the experimentalist, and the omission is of a proposer of the material platform. That is a real gap but not an arbitrary choice between peers. I agree that the fluctuation relations are exact and fundamental, and that a prize there would be well founded. Still, the experimental record is thinner and narrower, and I do not see enough support to make it a lead position.

responses.point: Pearce's two-part configuration pairs B024 with a sole-laureate B019 for Halzen, three laureates in total.
responses.response: I find the astronomy compelling, as I said in round 1, and I do not question the diffuse-flux discovery. I understand your note on the 4 to 5 sigma source associations, and I agree that the diffuse flux is the more secure result. But I cannot support Halzen alone, as the credit leaves out the AMANDA and IceCube builders and the protocol does not allow me to name them. On your structural question, a pairing of B044 and B024 would need five names, so it exceeds the three-person limit, and no two-part configuration I can see combines the strongest cases without that problem. That is why I keep a single part, and I would rather see B019 returned to later with a credit that fits.

uncertainties: I have not independently checked the priority chronology of Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, so my view that the HgTe proposal is an attribution gap rather than a priority problem rests on the first-round statements.
Whether Lindroth and Mehlig will hold that the 2016 prize reduces the novelty of time-reversal-invariant insulators; I think not, but that is a judgement and not a settled fact.

Whether the committee will treat the missing Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang as disqualifying relative to the clean two-name B024. I do not, but I recognise that reasonable members differ, and my own field is high-energy theory, not condensed matter, so I defer partly to Eriksson and Olsson on the materials literature.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with the shortlisted candidates is apparent from my profile. My documented connections (PhD supervisor David Gross, early mentor Hector Rubinstein, co-author Thomas Van Riet, the Uppsala theory group) are not among the credited names for B044, B024 or B020. My field is high-energy theory and cosmology, which limits my independent assessment of the topological insulator literature. I note Johansson's declared recusal on B042 and Kroll's flagged Boulder stay, and I do not think either changes the weight of the positions they state on B044 or B024.
